scope: Proposition 4.1 of the manuscript “Ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials” (preprints/Ultraflat-real-Littlewood-polynomials-October-5-2026/ultraflat-real-littlewood-polynomials.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 076 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 89e4fd2beb7f4dab), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every 0 < δ < 1/100, there are an integer m ≥ 2, a real trigonometric polynomial F on Tm, and v ∈ Rm with the following properties. Its Fourier support A ⊂ Zm \ {0} consists of at least two pairs {a, −a}, with distinct pairs nonparallel. If ca = b F(a), λa = a · v, wa = |λa|, then, for an absolute constant C, ∥F∥∞ ≤ 1 + δ, wa > 0, 1 − Cδ ≤ X a∈A wa < 1, 1 ≤ |ca| √ wa ≤ 1 + Cδ (a ∈ A). (4.1) The coefficient ratios in (4.1) are also at most 2.
